data.description: Found during the C11-192 stack-classification of Sentry issue C11-31: 96 of 875 captured hang events show main parked in a synchronous XPC reply wait (_dispatch_mach_send_and_wait_for_reply via LaunchServices/AppleEvents), with stall durations up to 604 seconds. This is a real wedge class distinct from SwiftUI graph work and generic-metadata instantiation: main is waiting on another process, and nothing bounds the wait. Counts are per-capture under the pre-#401 reporting regime and dominated by one user; recount per episode/per user before prioritizing (see C11-192 plan, Finding section). Work: identify the call sites that issue sync XPC from main (candidates: NSWorkspace/LaunchServices lookups, AppleEvents), move them off main or give them timeouts. Acceptance: the xpc-sync-wait Sentry issue (fingerprint main-thread-hang/xpc-sync-wait, exists once C11-192's classifier ships) shows a declining distinct-user count on the following release, and no capture exceeds 10s in that bucket.
data.title: Main thread blocks on synchronous XPC round trips (LaunchServices/AppleEvents), up to 604s

data.body:
Evidence pass (Sentry, 2600 unique events from C11-30/C11-31, filtered on xpc_connection_send_message_with_reply_sync / _dispatch_mach_send_and_wait_for_reply): 82 hits, 6 distinct users, four clusters.

  59 hits / 1 user  / max 142,654 ms : LS notification -> HIToolbox -> AESendMessage -> _LSCopyApplicationInformationItem
  12 hits / 5 users / max  16,264 ms : RunningBoard rbs_acquire_appnap_assertion via CFRunLoopSetOptionsReason
  10 hits / 3 users / max  48,908 ms : LS notification -> NSMenuBarDisplayManager _applicationNameChanged: -> NSRunningApplication.processIdentifier
   1 hit  / 1 user  / max  23,823 ms : c11 AppDelegate.syncMenuBarExtraVisibility -> NSRunningApplication.activationPolicy

Only one cluster carries a c11 frame:
  5 libxpc         xpc_connection_send_message_with_reply_sync
  7 LaunchServices _LSCopyApplicationInformation
  8 AppKit         -[NSRunningApplication _fetchDynamicProperties]
  9 AppKit         -[NSRunningApplication activationPolicy]
 10 c11            AppDelegate.syncMenuBarExtraVisibility(defaults:)
 11 c11            AppDelegate.installMenuBarVisibilityObserver()...

Sentry truncates captured stacks at 24 frames, so the other clusters bottom out in the event loop before a c11 frame could appear. Audited the same call shape across Sources/ instead of guessing, which found three more LaunchServices lookups on hot main-thread paths.

Confirmed c11-owned sync-XPC call sites, all fixed:
1. AppDelegate.syncMenuBarExtraVisibility -> NSApp.activationPolicy(). Runs on every UserDefaults.didChangeNotification. Now reads AppPresentationPolicy.effectiveActivationPolicy(), which serves the policy c11 itself set (apply() is the only setActivationPolicy call site), plus a short-circuit when the answer already matches the installed state.
2. ContentView.resolveCommandPaletteTerminalOpenTargets -> TerminalDirectoryOpenTarget.availableTargets(). Rebuilt on every command-palette keystroke; each of 14 targets not found on disk falls back to NSWorkspace.fullPath(forApplication:). Now availableTargetsCached(): 60s TTL, refresh on a utility queue, blocking probe only on the first call in a process.
3. DraggableFolderIconRepresentable.updateNSView -> NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:). Fired on every SwiftUI update pass for the sidebar, plus every drag start and path-menu popup. Now FolderIconCache (memoized by path, 5 min TTL, NSCache) and the representable only re-resolves when the path actually changed.
4. SettingsView.refreshDetectedImportBrowsers -> InstalledBrowserDetector (a dozen NSWorkspace.urlForApplication probes) on main from .onAppear. Now detached, matching BrowserPanelView.
5. TabManager pre-modal NSApp.activationPolicy(). Same LS round trip, rare path, now reads the recorded policy.

New Sources/ExpiringValueCache.swift is the shared seam: TTL cache with injectable monotonic clock, serves the previous value immediately when stale and hands the recompute to a caller-supplied scheduler.

Deliberately left alone:
- The other 81 evidence hits. System-owned LaunchServices notification deliveries into c11's idle runloop, plus RunningBoard app-nap assertions. No c11 frame, no c11 call, nothing on our side can bound them.
- TerminalController.v2AwaitCallback main-thread branch. Already slices CFRunLoopRunInMode against a caller deadline; the one hit naming it is cluster A's LS notification running inside that pump.
- NSWorkspace.shared.open(...) sites (~25). Synchronous, but one shot per explicit action with the Bool consumed inline; converting them all changes the contract for no measured gain.
- enforceSingleInstance runningApplications lookup (launch-time, once) and NSOpenPanel/NSSavePanel (user-driven modals, sync by design).

Acceptance-criterion caveat: "no capture exceeds 10s in that bucket" is not reachable by fixing c11 call sites, because 81 of 82 captures are the OS blocking our main thread in an idle runloop with no c11 frame. Recommend re-scoping to the c11-attributable subset, or teaching the xpc-sync-wait rule in MainThreadHangMonitor to split "c11 frame present" from "system-owned LS notification delivery" so the bucket measures something we control.

Tests: c11Tests/ExpiringValueCacheTests.swift, wired into the c11LogicTests target. Behavioral with an injected clock: TTL semantics, coalesced background refresh, and 50 simulated palette keystrokes issuing exactly one LaunchServices probe pass (counted through the injected DetectionEnvironment). No test added for FolderIconCache or the updateNSView guard: the property that matters is "no XPC on the render path", not observable without an injection seam on an NSView subclass a bare xctest runner cannot construct reliably.

PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/414 (branch fix/C11-196-xpc-sync-main). Not built locally per the no-local-xcodebuild rule; CI is the gate.

PR #414 merged to main 2026-08-12 (squash), all CI green. Validated on a real tagged build before merge, not on CI alone, because three of the five changed sites are user-visible and caching is exactly the change that passes tests and then shows a human a stale value.

Tagged build c11-196-validate from commit 645475730, launched with launch-tagged-automation.sh --qa fresh. All five checks PASS. The operator's production c11 was untouched throughout; the driver aborted rather than typing whenever the tagged build was not verified frontmost, which it did once.

CACHE INVALIDATION PROVEN LIVE, BOTH DIRECTIONS. The availableTargetsCached 60s TTL was probed with a reversible stub ~/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app carrying an executable code-tunnel: the two VS Code Inline Server commands appeared within the TTL and disappeared again after the stub was removed. So the cache is neither stale-forever nor fabricating availability. Stub removed and verified gone.

FOLDER ICON memoization invalidates on path change: four distinct paths gave four distinct correct icons, and the icon follows a focus change between panes with different cwds. No memoization leak.

ACTIVATION POLICY substitution proven correct by inference rather than assertion: with the menu bar pref off, had effectiveActivationPolicy() returned .accessory instead of .regular, shouldInstallMenuBarExtra would have been true unconditionally and the glyph would have appeared. It did not. That is the specific regression the swap risked, and it is ruled out.

SETTINGS BROWSER DETECTION populates on a cold process at first poll, 2.29s after the menu click including ~1.2s of the harness's own overhead. No perceptible empty state from the detach.

SANITY: no crashes, zero hang or fatal lines in the debug log, terminals echo and execute normally, 4.3% CPU, no beachball.

Two pre-existing issues recorded but not introduced by this PR: the palette's 'Open in X' entries are not gated on install status so it offers editors that are not installed, and showMenuBarExtra has no Settings UI and needs a relaunch.

Worktree and branch cleaned up.

ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE DECLARED VOID, TRANSFERRED TO C11-208 (same treatment C11-191's repro clause got when it moved to C11-202).

The clause read: 'the xpc-sync-wait Sentry issue shows a declining distinct-user count on the following release, and no capture exceeds 10s in that bucket.' It cannot be satisfied by fixing c11 code. 81 of the 82 xpc-sync-wait captures in the corpus are the OS blocking our main thread with no c11 frame present: LaunchServices notification deliveries into an idle runloop (59 captures, one user, max 142,654 ms) and RunningBoard app-nap assertions (12 captures, 5 users). Removing every sync XPC call c11 makes would leave those numbers untouched. The bucket does not currently measure anything we own, which is the real defect, and C11-208 owns fixing that.

WHAT THIS TICKET ACTUALLY DELIVERED, and it stands on its own: five confirmed main-thread sync-XPC call sites removed, two of them on paths that fired constantly and had never appeared in Sentry at all. The command palette rebuilt 14 editor-availability probes on every keystroke, each miss falling through to NSWorkspace.fullPath(forApplication:); the sidebar folder icon called NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:) on every SwiftUI update pass. Those are the finds that justify the ticket, and they came from auditing the call shape rather than from the Sentry evidence, because the 24-frame wire truncation hid them.

Methodology note worth carrying forward: the Sentry evidence named one call site. The code audit found four more. On a truncated-stack corpus, treat the evidence as a starting point that proves the class is real, not as the enumeration of its members.

Merged as PR #414, validated on a tagged build (see the validation comment above).
